Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed mass with homogeneous opacity in the right upper lung field, which lacks the spiculated margins typical of bronchogenic carcinoma or the air-fluid levels of an abscess. This radiographic appearance, combined with the massive size seen on CT, is characteristic of pleuropulmonary synovial sarcoma (PPSS), a rare soft tissue sarcoma that often presents as a large, well-defined intrathoracic mass.
